description: Automatic package updates (story E01-004). Updates wait seven days after release, the same rule as uv and pnpm.

packageRules.description: Minor and patch updates merge themselves when every check passes.
Major updates wait for a review.
GitHub Actions updates are grouped into one pull request.
A uv update can change _virtualenv.py, whose hash is in tools/startup-files-allowed.txt, so updates to the uv program and the uv image are reviewed before they are merged.
dependency-cruiser cannot read TypeScript 7.0, so the client stays on TypeScript 6 until 7.1.
Container images are pinned by digest. The tag is kept next to the digest so that people can see the version.
Chromium for the browser tests comes from Playwright's image, which has to match the version of @playwright/test, so the two are updated together.
Updates to source code built in the Dockerfiles are reviewed before they are merged, because the version is also written in the build flags of the same stage, and Renovate does not update those.

The socket proxy image on lscr.io is published on Docker Hub as linuxserver/socket-proxy with the same digests, so versions and digests are looked up there, and the seven-day rule is applied. The socket proxy can reach the Docker socket, so its updates are reviewed before they are merged.
The uv image on ghcr.io is published on Docker Hub as astral/uv with the same digests, so versions and digests are looked up there, and the seven-day rule is applied.

Renovate has release dates for Docker Hub only, and Playwright's image is on mcr.microsoft.com alone, so the seven-day rule cannot be applied to it. Its updates are reviewed before they are merged, and an update cannot be merged before the matching @playwright/test update, which waits seven days, because the two versions are compared in infra/tests/test_browser_image.py.
The Tailscale image and the Tailscale source built in the same Dockerfile are updated together, and reviewed.
The Caddy images and the Caddy version built with xcaddy are updated together, and reviewed.
Node.js in the pipeline (.nvmrc) and in caddy.Dockerfile are updated together.

Renovate cannot read a hash for Pester from the PowerShell Gallery, so its version is updated by Renovate and its hash in tools/programs.txt with tools/update_pester_hash.py (docs/package-updates.md). The job "Server, contracts and tools" fails until the hash is updated.

Programs that run in the release job, check signatures or check the code (Grype, Syft, gitleaks, PSScriptAnalyzer, Pester and the installer's cosign) are reviewed by a person before they are merged, after the seven-day wait.
A new hash for a program without a new version means that the release file was replaced, so it is not merged by Renovate.

customManagers.description: The uv version in required-version in pyproject.toml, marked with a renovate comment.
Images in Python scripts, marked with a renovate comment and pinned by digest, as in the Dockerfiles.
Images named in the workflows, marked with a renovate comment.
Source code cloned in the Dockerfiles: the release tag and the commit it is checked against.
The Caddy version built with xcaddy, which has to match the Caddy images in the same Dockerfile.

cosign, downloaded by the installer: the version in the address, and the SHA-256 on the next line. Renovate finds the file with that hash in the current release, and writes the hash of the same file in the new release. The download is checked against the hash in the Container bundle job.

Programs from GitHub releases in tools/programs.txt, pinned by the SHA-256 of the release file. Renovate finds the file with that hash in the current release, and writes the hash of the same file in the new release.
PowerShell modules from the PowerShell Gallery in tools/programs.txt. Renovate updates the version. The hash is updated with tools/update_pester_hash.py (docs/package-updates.md).
